applicable_when: The kernel uses BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=32 with 128 threads (4 warps). The B matrix has stride_bk=1, stride_bn=512, meaning B is stored column-major for N. When tl.dot stages the [BLOCK_K=32, BLOCK_N=128] B-tile through shared memory, threads reading along the N-dimension access elements with stride 512 in global memory, and the resulting SMEM layout causes 8-way bank conflicts. The 168 registers/thread is the direct consequence of holding BLOCK_M*BLOCK_N=8192 accumulator elements plus tile buffers, capping occupancy at 3 blocks/SM. Reducing BLOCK_N from 128 to 64 halves the accumulator size (8192 to 4096 elements), cutting registers to ~100/thread and allowing 4-6 blocks/SM. Simultaneously increasing BLOCK_K from 32 to 64 halves K-loop iterations (16 to 8), reducing loop overhead and changing the SMEM tile geometry so the 64-wide N dimension aligns better with the 32-bank SMEM layout, reducing bank conflicts. This is a pure constexpr tile-size change with no algorithmic or index-logic modification, avoiding the correctness failures seen in prior attempts.
